wires.title: Hidden wires
wires.intro: Under its insulation, every wire carries a tag: one letter and one digit, such as K7. The Scanner can read the tags. The Operator sees the wire colors and the serial number on the case. Count wires from the top, starting at 1.
wires.step1: Step 1. Find the key color from the last digit of the serial number.
wires.step2: Step 2. If two or more wires are the key color, those wires are the candidates. Otherwise, every wire that is not the key color is a candidate.
wires.step3: Step 3. Look for candidates whose tag letter also appears in the serial number. If there are any, cut the one among them whose tag has the highest digit. If there are none, cut the candidate whose tag has the lowest digit.
wires.unique: No two tags on one bomb share a digit, so exactly one wire fits. Cutting any other wire is a strike.

keypad.title: Glyph keypad
keypad.intro: The keypad has four keys, numbered 1 to 4 from the left. Each key carries a glyph: a frame (circle, triangle, square or arch) with a mark inside (dot, two dots, upright line, flat line, X or caret). The Operator sees the glyphs and the serial number. The Scanner sees which key is live.
keypad.step1: Step 1. Find the ring below that holds three or four of the keypad's glyphs. A key whose glyph is not in that ring is a dud: never press it.
keypad.step2: Step 2. Press the live key first.
keypad.step3: Step 3. From the live key's glyph, walk around its ring: toward higher positions if the first digit of the serial number is even, toward lower positions if it is odd. The ring wraps: after the last position comes position 1, and before position 1 comes the last. Press each key as you reach its glyph, until every key except a dud is pressed.
keypad.strike: Pressing a key out of turn is a strike. Keys already pressed stay pressed.

dial.title: Frequency dial
dial.intro: The Scanner sees a waveform on the dial's screen. The Operator turns the dial, reads the frequency on its display and presses Send.
dial.step1: Step 1. Match the waveform's shape below, then take the base frequency from the column that fits the serial number.
dial.withoutAE: Serial has no A or E
dial.step2: Step 2. Add 6 for each peak on the screen. A flat top counts as one peak.
dial.step3: Step 3. If the peaks only reach the dashed middle line, not the solid top line, subtract 9.
dial.strike: Send the result. Sending any other frequency is a strike.
